title: Digits Erase the Letter Before
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters and digits. Each digit works like a backspace key: it removes itself together with the closest letter to its left that has not been removed yet.

Apply this for every digit and return the letters that remain, in their original order. The input is guaranteed to always have a letter available for each digit.

examples.why: The 1 removes the b right before it.
The first 2 removes r. The second 2's nearest remaining letter to the left is now q, not r again.

constraints: s has lowercase letters and digits
Every digit has an unremoved letter somewhere to its left
hints: Think of typing the string into a text box where each digit is a backspace.
The letter a digit removes is always the most recently kept letter. Which structure gives you the most recent item?
Push letters onto a stack; on a digit, pop. Join the stack at the end.

explain.intuition:
This is a text box with backspace. Each digit deletes the last letter that is still on screen. "Last thing kept, first thing removed" is a stack: push each letter, pop on each digit.

Deleting characters from the middle of a string in a loop costs O(n) per deletion, so the naive version is O(n²). The stack does each step in O(1), and the final join is O(n).
steps: Create an empty stack (an array of characters).
For each character: if it is a digit, pop the stack; otherwise push the letter.
Join the stack into a string and return it.
pitfalls: Removing the character at a fixed position (like i − 1) instead of the nearest remaining letter. In "pqr22x" the second 2 must remove q.
Building the result with repeated string slicing, which is quadratic on long inputs.

solutions.title: Delete from the string directly
solutions.idea: Find the first digit, cut it and the character before it out of the string, and repeat.

solutions.title: Stack of letters
solutions.idea: Push letters, pop on digits. What is left on the stack is the answer.

followups: Each digit d removes the d nearest letters instead of one. What changes?
Do it in place on a character array with O(1) extra space.
